correctness.rationale: PASS: For grid X=product of chains of lengths q_i>=2, pair-interval closure generates the coordinatewise extrema box by meet/join. Every nonclosed pair is a recursive pseudo-intent; larger pseudo-intents are impossible because all constituent pair boxes must be contained. Every valid basis needs one distinct first-firing premise per nonclosed pair; counting nonclosed pairs as all unordered pairs less Cartesian adjacent edges gives the global minimum rule count. For target point z an inclusion-minimal support has <=d seeds for d>=2, each essential seed uniquely charged to a coordinate. Balanced two-block interval merging gives ceil(log2 d) synchronous rounds, and binary unit vectors force that many rounds. d=1 cases checked separately. Direct independent enumeration of 5 small grids, including 256 initial sets for the three-cube, matched every closure and depth. No finite test was treated as all-grid proof.
